Extract ALL references to components from this document.

COMPONENTS: WebUI, Registry, Persistence, Recommender, Auth, SlopeOneRecommender, OrderBasedRecommender, DummyRecommender, PopularityBasedRecommender, ImageProvider, PreprocessedSlopeOneRecommender


Include a reference when the sentence refers to the component by name, alias, or as a participant in a described interaction. Exclude when the name appears only inside a code-level path — even if the compound identifier is semantically related to the component — or as ordinary English with no architectural intent. Favor inclusion.

DOCUMENT:
S1: The TeaStore consists of 5 replicatable services and a single Registry instance.
S2: The WebUI service retrieves images from the Image Provider.
S3: Users are authenticated by the Auth service.
S4: Data is retrieved from the PersistenceProvider and product recommendations from the Recommender service.
S5: The WebUI provides the TeaStore front-end using Servlets in combination with JSP files.
S6: It contains logic to save and retireve values from cookies.
S7: Images (with few exceptions) are not provides by the WebUi, but are retrieved from the Image Provider service instead.
S8: The UI provides a status page at link indicating the current state of the TeaStore.
S9: The status view lists the instance count and hosts for all registered service instances.
S10: The Image Provider delivers images to the WebUI as base64 encoded strings to embed them in the final HTML.
S11: It matches the provided product ID or UI name (the filename for images not representing a product and therefore without product ID) and the image size to a unique image identifier.
S12: If the product ID or UI name is not available to the Image Provider, a standard "not found" image will be delivered in the correct size.
S13: If the product ID or UI name is found but not in the requested size, the largest image will be loaded and scaled.
S14: The scaled image is stored for later use.
S15: If the product ID or UI name and size is found, the image will be loaded and delivered.
S16: To speed up image delivery, an in-memory cache with Least Frequently Used (LFU) replacemenent strategy is in place.
S17: Before loading an image from the physical drive, a cache lookup will be performed and if the image is present, delivered directly from cache or from the physical drive otherwise.
S18: The Auth service handles user and session authentication.
S19: Passwords are hashed using BCrypt.
S20: To validate sessions, the SessionBlob is salted and hashed using SHA512 and stored in a cookie.
S21: When a SessionBlob is received, the cookie content is re-salted and checked against the hash to check for session tampering.
S22: The Persistence service provides access to the data persisted in the relational database back-end.
S23: It maps the relational entities to the JSON entity objects passed between services using the EclipseLink JPA ORM mapper.
S24: It features endpoints for general CRUD-Operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete) for the persistent entities.
S25: The persistence provider uses a second level entity cache provided by the JPA implementation.
S26: As such, it also acts as a caching layer.
S27: The Recommender is used to generate individual product recommendations for each user.
S28: It is trained using all existing orders.
S29: Recommendations are generated based on the users current shopping cart, the user's previous orders and/or the item the user is currently looking at.
S30: The item rating of the users are based on their purchases.
S31: If the current user is unknown (e.g., if the user is not logged in or did not purchase anything yet), a fallback algorithm based on the general item popularity is chosen.
S32: If the user is known, Slope One as item-based collaborative filtering is applied to calculate the recommendations.
S33: We implemented two versions of the algorithm.
S34: One CPU-intensive, calculating the item-rankings per user on-the-go and one memory-intensive, calculating the total user rating prediction matrix during the training phase.
S35: Furthermore, one order-based nearest-neighbor approach is available.
S36: Its recommendation time is dependent on the number of items in the current cart as well as the total number of stored orders.
S37: The Registry provides information about how many service instances are online for each service and where they are located.
S38: Service instances register themselves at the registry on startup.
S39: Services are also required to send a heartbeat signal by re-registering periodically.
S40: Services missing their heartbeat for more than 10 s are assumed to be offline until the register function is called again.
S41: Every running instance of the TeaStore uses one single registry.
S42: The TeaStore is a test application.
S43: By limiting it to a single registry instance, it enables easy configuration of multiple parallel TeaStores with minimal configuration overhead.
